current_specification:
Setting terminal window title

## Type of changes

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation / docstrings
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Other

## Checklist

- [x] I've run the latest [black](https://github.com/psf/black) with default args on new code.
- [x] I've updated CHANGELOG.md and CONTRIBUTORS.md where appropriate.
- [x] I've added tests for new code.
- [x] I accept that @willmcgugan may be pedantic in the code review.

## Description

Adds support for setting the title of the terminal window.

There is no means within Rich of "resetting" the window title to its
previous value, meaning the title you set will persist even after your application
exists.

`fish` shell resets the window title before and after each command by default,
negating this issue. Windows Terminal and command prompt will also reset the title for you.
Most other shells and terminals, however, do not do this.

Some terminals may require configuration changes before you can set the title.
Some terminals may not support setting the title at all.

Other software (including the terminal itself, the shell, custom prompts, plugins, etc.)
may also set the terminal window title. This could result in whatever value you write
using this method being overwritten.

Title sanitization is done in the Control factory (rich/control.py:81-82), keeping control-code policy out of Console.
Nuance only: str.isprintable at rich/control.py:81 also strips Unicode Cf/Zs characters such as ZWJ and NBSP, which the reference does not do. This is a behavior choice, not a boundary violation.
rich/console.py:1143-1152 show_cursor and rich/console.py:1168-1172 set_alt_screen gate on is_terminal (set_alt_screen also checks legacy_windows) and return bool.
Candidate rich/console.py:1049-1057 has no is_terminal gate and returns None.
bell() at rich/console.py:1045-1047 is ungated, so the candidate follows that precedent, but the terminal-state setters use the gated, bool-returning pattern that the reference follows.
CHANGELOG.md:10-12 placement and docstring style follow repository conventions (pass).
criteria.deficiency: Terminal-only setter does not follow the gated bool-return convention used by show_cursor and set_alt_screen.

evidence: Core emission works: rich/control.py:33 yields '\x1b]0;{title}\x07' and rich/console.py:1057 writes it via self.control, so POSIX/VT terminals receive the title change.
Legacy Windows gap: rich/_windows_renderer.py is unchanged and rich/console.py:1935-1948 routes control segments there, so the title is silently dropped (see extension_registration).

Non-terminal record leak: rich/console.py:1925-1926 extends _record_buffer with every buffered segment, including control segments; rich/console.py:2050-2053 export_text(styles=True) joins raw text of segments with style None, so a record=True non-terminal console would include the raw OSC sequence. The reference avoids this with its is_terminal guard (reference.diff console.py). bell() shares this latent behavior, so this is a divergence from the reference rather than from every precedent.
Return value: no success signal (console.py:1049), unlike the reference's bool contract.

By reading only: the reference's windows-renderer test (reference.diff tests/test_windows_renderer.py) asserts set_title is called; the candidate has no branch for it, so that behavior would not hold. Absent tests are not counted as deletions.
criteria.deficiency: Feature partly meets intent: it emits the title sequence for modern terminals but fails on legacy Windows, returns no success status, and can leak the escape into exported text for recording consoles.
